entries.name: Indus Valley (Harappan) civilization
entries.region: Indus basin, modern Pakistan and NW India
entries.settlement: planned grid cities of fired brick with drains and wells
trade: lapis lazuli and tin from Afghanistan
entries.beliefs: undeciphered; mother-goddess figurines, bull icons, no temples identified
entries.fell_by: Ghaggar-Hakra river dried up, climate shifted east, towns emptied into villages
entries.notes: The most city-sized Bronze Age neighbor to Mesopotamia: uniform bricks and drains over 1000 km. Model grid towns, wells and granaries before palaces.

entries.name: Vedic culture
entries.region: Punjab, then the upper Gangetic plain
entries.settlement: clan villages around fire altars; tribal assemblies
trade: river trade along the Indus and Ganges
entries.beliefs: Rigvedic gods - Indra, Agni, Varuna; sacrifice and cosmic order (rita)
entries.fell_by: gave way to the mahajanapadas and Upanishadic thought
entries.notes: No walls before the cities: model as seasonal cattle-camps and fire-altar villages, not towns. The naming pool for heroic Hindu names.

entries.name: Maurya Empire
entries.region: Gangetic plain and most of the subcontinent
entries.settlement: walled imperial cities with a monumental palace and treasury core
entries.beliefs: Buddhism after Ashoka's conversion; Brahminism and Jainism tolerated
entries.fell_by: weak successors and the Shunga coup under Pushyamitra, 185 BCE
entries.notes: Asia's first empire of continental scale; the game's 'unified India' template and the source of pillar and stupa monuments.

entries.name: Gupta Empire
entries.settlement: small walled towns and prosperous villages under craft guilds
trade: spices and cotton to Rome then SE Asia
entries.beliefs: Hinduism, especially Vaishnavism; temple worship flourished
entries.fell_by: Huna (Hephthalite) invasions and internal fragmentation
entries.notes: The classical age: zero notation, algebra and great epics copied. Use for 'golden age' tech tier and temple-town building.

entries.name: Chola Empire
entries.region: Coromandel coast and the Tamil country
entries.settlement: temple-centered market towns and tank-irrigated villages
trade: cotton textiles and spices to SE Asia and China
naval expeditions to Sri Lanka and the Straits
entries.beliefs: Shaivism centered on the great temples
entries.fell_by: Pandya revolts and fragmentation into regional chieftaincies
entries.notes: The seafaring Indian empire; bronzes and temple tanks are its visual signature - the game's 'temple-port' bioregion.

entries.name: Mughal Empire
entries.region: North India and later the Deccan
entries.settlement: great walled capitals and garden cities
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam; later emperors varied in policy toward Hindu subjects
entries.fell_by: East India Company annexations, the revolt of 1857, last emperor exiled to Rangoon
entries.notes: The reference 'grand monumental India': white marble, charbagh gardens, red-sandstone forts. Instant voxel skyline material.

entries.name: Delhi Sultanate
entries.settlement: walled garrison capitals with congregational mosques
monuments: Qutb Minar and the Alai Darwaza, Delhi
crafts: paper currency experiments under Muhammad bin Tughluq
trade: horses from Arabia and Central Asia
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam ruling a Hindu-majority country
entries.fell_by: Timur's sack of Delhi in 1398 weakened it; Babur crushed it at Panipat, 1526
entries.notes: Turkic-Afghan military aristocracy holding the Gangetic plain by cavalry and fortresses; India's first lasting Islamic polity.

entries.name: Vijayanagara Empire
entries.settlement: vast planned temple-bazaar capital at Hampi
trade: horses for its cavalry from Arabia
entries.beliefs: Hindu Shaivite-Vaishnavite synthesis under royal patronage
entries.fell_by: defeat at Talikota in 1565; the court fled Hampi and a rump dynasty ruled to 1646
entries.notes: A city of a few hundred thousand at its peak; its ruins are a ready-made massive voxel site - one of the great lost-city set pieces.

entries.name: Rajput clans
entries.settlement: hill forts above arid plains, clan hamlets below
entries.beliefs: Hindu deity-centered clan temples (Eklingji, Karni Mata); honor and loyalty codes
entries.fell_by: Mughal domination from the 1560s, then subsidiary alliances with the British by 1818
entries.notes: Honor-bound warrior aristocracy; their forts double as palaces - dramatic silhouette blocks for high-ground builds.

entries.name: Maratha Confederacy
entries.region: the Western Ghats heartland, then most of the subcontinent
entries.settlement: mountain fort-capitals (Raigad, Pratapgad) and new bazaar towns
entries.beliefs: Hindu devotional revival; Shivaji patron of Bhavani and Hanuman
entries.fell_by: Third Anglo-Maratha War, 1817-18
entries.notes: Fast fort-to-fort light-cavalry power; the counterpoint empire to Mughal Delhi - mobile, guerrilla, plateau-bred.

entries.name: Sikh Empire
entries.region: the Panjab and beyond the Khyber
entries.settlement: cantonment cities (Lahore, Amritsar) around Sikh gurdwaras
entries.beliefs: Sikhism, the Khalsa order
entries.fell_by: Anglo-Sikh Wars 1845-49; annexed by the British in 1849
entries.notes: The last sovereign Panjab kingdom; disciplined Khalsa cavalry and artillery - a mobile, reforming state, over in fifty years.

entries.name: Sangam Tamil culture
entries.region: the Tamil country, Kaveri delta to Vaigai
entries.settlement: port cities (Puhar, Korkai, Muziris) and agricultural delta villages
trade: spices and pearls to Rome and Arabia
entries.beliefs: Murugan-centered worship, hero stones, early Tamil devotion
entries.fell_by: evolved into the Pallava and early Chola age
entries.notes: A literature-rich coast-and-delta civilization; the source of spice-market flavor, pearl blocks and Tamil name pools.

entries.name: Mahajanapadas (Magadha and the rest)
entries.region: the upper Gangetic plain and Bihar
entries.settlement: the first large fortified towns (Rajgir, Pataliputra) and republics (Vajji, Malla)
entries.beliefs: Jainism, Buddhism, Ajivikas, Vedic Brahmanism - all born or reshaped here
entries.fell_by: unified under Magadha, then the Maurya conquest in 321 BCE
entries.notes: The sixteen-state era: cities, coins and new religions all appear at once - historians call it the second urbanization.

entries.name: Kushan Empire
entries.settlement: caravan cities on the Silk Road (Taxila, Peshawar, Mathura)
trade: Silk Road relay: horses, spices, silk and monks
entries.beliefs: Buddhism (Mahayana), Zoroastrian elements, steppe sky-god cults
entries.fell_by: Sassanian invasions and Gupta pressure; broke into small kingdoms
entries.notes: Where Greek, Persian and Indian art fuse into the first Buddha statues - the game's ultimate 'crossroads' culture.

entries.name: Satavahana dynasty
entries.settlement: fortified towns and hill monasteries carved from rock (Karle, Nasik)
trade: pepper and spices via western ports (Barygaza)
entries.beliefs: Buddhism patronized; Brahmin ritual retained at court
entries.fell_by: successor states (Abhiras, Ikshvakus) and Western Kshatrapa rivalry
entries.notes: The Deccan's bridge-builders of the spice trade; why west coast digs turn up Roman coin hoards.

entries.name: Pallava dynasty
entries.settlement: port towns and temple capitals (Kanchipuram, Mamallapuram)
entries.beliefs: Shaivism and Vaishnavism; patrons of the bhakti hymn writers
entries.fell_by: Chalukya and Chola wars; Aditya Chola annexed Tondaimandalam
entries.notes: Invented the freestanding stone temple in South India; the step between rock caves and Chola granite.

entries.name: Chalukya dynasties (Badami and Western)
entries.settlement: stone-temple capitals (Badami, Aihole, Pattadakal, Kalyani)
entries.beliefs: Hinduism across sects; Jain shrines tolerated
entries.fell_by: Rashtrakutas overthrew the Badami line in 753; Cholas and Hoysalas displaced the Westerns
entries.notes: Vesara temple style born here; Pulakeshin II famously stopped Harsha on the Narmada - two empires meet at a river.

entries.name: Rashtrakuta Empire
entries.region: the Deccan and much of central India
entries.settlement: rock-cut patronage centers and tent-and-garden courts (Manyakheta, Ellora)
entries.beliefs: Hinduism; Kailasa dedicated to Shiva, with generous patronage of Jains and Buddhists
entries.fell_by: Tailapa II of the Western Chalukyas wrested Manyakheta in 973
entries.notes: Kailasa temple is a whole mountain carved downward - about 200,000 tonnes of rock removed; the ultimate voxel set piece.

entries.name: Pala Empire
climate: Cfa/Aw wet delta and Gangetic east
entries.settlement: rice-rich delta towns and Buddhist monastery-universities (Nalanda, Vikramashila)
entries.beliefs: Mahayana Buddhism; Hindu Tantric cults also flourished
entries.fell_by: Sena dynasty takeover, then Muslim expansion into Bihar and Bengal
entries.notes: Bengal's Buddhist university-empire and the channel by which Buddhism reached Tibet; ideal for eastern-marsh settings.

entries.name: Hoysala Empire
entries.settlement: star-shaped temple-towns (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura)
entries.beliefs: Vaishnavism and Shaivism under one crown; Jain temples also built
entries.fell_by: Sultanate of Madurai raids, then absorption into Vijayanagara
entries.notes: The most ornate temples in India - floor-to-ceiling soapstone friezes; a showcase build for interior detail.

entries.name: Harsha's empire
entries.settlement: an itinerant royal court - Harsha never stayed in one capital
crafts: Sanskrit drama (he wrote three plays himself)
entries.beliefs: Shiva and Buddha both; he hosted councils of each
entries.fell_by: died without an adult heir in 647; the empire dissolved at once
entries.notes: One man's personal empire; the Chinese pilgrim Xuanzang visited and wrote it down - a rare first-person source.

entries.name: Indo-Greek kingdoms
entries.settlement: Greek-style towns with gymnasia and agoras (Taxila)
entries.beliefs: Greek gods syncretized with Indian ones; Heliodorus styled himself a Bhagavata
entries.fell_by: Indo-Scythian conquest; kings absorbed into the Saka-Pahlava mix
entries.notes: Greek kings who took up Buddhism (the Milinda Panha dialogues) - an unexpected but documented East-meets-West fusion.

entries.name: Indo-Scythians (Sakas / Western Kshatrapas)
entries.region: west and northwest India, Ujjain and Junagadh
entries.settlement: frontier fort-towns and caravan capitals (Ujjain)
monuments: Junagadh rock inscription of Rudradaman I
entries.beliefs: Saka sun-worship (Surya) assimilated into Hindu cults
entries.fell_by: Gupta conquest - Chandragupta II ended the Western Kshatrapas in about 400 CE
entries.notes: Horse-archer steppe lords who went native fast; the source of the Saka era, still used in the Indian national calendar.

entries.name: Anuradhapura kingdom
entries.region: the lowland dry zone of Sri Lanka
entries.settlement: tank-and-canal irrigation capitals; one of Asia's largest cities of its age
dwellings: stilt houses in the wet zone
monuments: Sri Maha Bodhi (cutting from the Buddha's tree)
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism - guardian of the Pali canon
entries.fell_by: Chola conquest under Rajaraja I (993-1017); the capital shifted to Polonnaruwa
entries.notes: An irrigation civilization: a city of around 100,000 sustained by artificial reservoirs - a waterworks wonder for the game.

entries.name: Bahmani Sultanate
entries.region: the Deccan, from Gulbarga then Bidar
entries.settlement: walled twin capitals with Persianate court culture
monuments: Bidar fort and its Rangin Mahal
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam; Sufi saints (like Zinda Pir) were beloved of the court
entries.fell_by: broke into five Deccan sultanates: Bijapur, Golconda, Bidar, Berar, Ahmednagar
entries.notes: The Deccan's Persianate counterweight to the north, in constant war with Vijayanagara - two rival high cultures one plateau.

entries.name: Bengal Sultanate
entries.settlement: river-port capitals (Sonargaon, Pandua, Gaur)
monuments: Shat Gombuj (Sixty Dome) Mosque at Bagerhat
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam with deep Sufi influence; local cults absorbed into Islam
entries.fell_by: Mughal conquest completed in 1576 with the fall of Rajmahal
entries.notes: Home of the world's finest muslin; a creek-and-delta terrain that reads completely differently from the Gangetic plain.

entries.name: Kashmir Sultanate
entries.settlement: walled valley towns (Srinagar) and terraced orchards
dwellings: timber and deodar houses with carved balconies
entries.beliefs: Islam via Rinchan Shah; Hindu court pandits retained influence under Zain-ul-Abidin
entries.fell_by: annexed by the Mughals in 1586; later Afghan Durrani then Sikh rule
entries.notes: A valley artisan economy - shawls and saffron; luxury exports with a very small footprint, perfect for a pocket realm.

entries.name: Ahom kingdom
entries.settlement: stilted villages and moated capitals (Charaideo, Garhgaon)
dwellings: stilt houses of the Assam type
monuments: maidams - the royal burial mounds at Charaideo
entries.beliefs: Ahom ancestor worship fused with Hinduism (Shiva), later Shakta devotion
entries.fell_by: Burmese occupation, then British annexation at the Treaty of Yandabo, 1826
entries.notes: Fought off the Mughals for six centuries with riverine guerrilla war; the maidams are stepped burial mounds - South Asia's own pyramids.

entries.name: Newar culture of the Kathmandu Valley (Licchavi-Malla)
entries.settlement: brick-and-timber market towns around palace squares (Kathmandu, Patan, Bhaktapur)
dwellings: brick courtyard houses with carved timber windows
monuments: Kathmandu, Patan and Bhaktapur Durbar Squares
entries.beliefs: Vajrayana Buddhism and Shaiva Hinduism fused into one civic religion
entries.fell_by: conquered by the Gorkha king Prithvi Narayan Shah in 1768-69
entries.notes: Living medieval craft-towns with palace squares; one of the few places where a Malla-era streetscape still stands daily.

entries.name: Kingdom of Kandy
entries.region: the central highlands of Sri Lanka
entries.settlement: a forest citadel around the Temple of the Tooth
monuments: Temple of the Sacred Tooth Relic
entries.beliefs: Theravada Buddhism; the Tooth relic as the state palladium
entries.fell_by: Kandyan Convention with the British in 1815; the last king exiled to Vellore
entries.notes: Sri Lanka's 'last free highland kingdom'; misty ridgeline fortress-capital, relic-centered - a compact, dramatic set piece.

entries.name: Sultanate of Maldives
entries.settlement: coral-stone island towns and mosques
dwellings: coral-stone mosques with carved lacquer ceilings
trade: cowries exported as coin to Bengal and Africa
entries.beliefs: Sunni Islam, adopted in 1153 under Koimala
entries.fell_by: became a republic briefly in 1953, again for good in 1968 - 815 years of sultanate
entries.notes: A coral-atoll dhow economy; if the game has ocean islands, this is their inhabited culture - salt, coconut and cowries.

entries.name: Mehrgarh culture
entries.settlement: mudbrick multi-room farmsteads guarding the Bolan Pass route
entries.beliefs: burials with grave goods; no texts; pre-religious iconography unknown
entries.fell_by: grew directly into the Indus civilization's Baluchistan phase
entries.notes: Seven thousand years of continuous farming - South Asia's 'first village', and the deepest root of Harappan urbanism.

entries.name: South Indian megalith builders
entries.region: southern India and its Sri Lankan fringes
entries.settlement: open agricultural villages beside urn and dolmen burial grounds
entries.beliefs: ancestor cults; pantheon unknown
entries.fell_by: absorbed into the Sangam-age kingdoms; the burial rite faded
entries.notes: Iron Age grave-builders under every South Indian hill; reads visually as dolmens and standing stones - cheap blocks, big presence.

entries.name: Gond kingdoms (Garha-Katanga, Deogarh, Chanda)
entries.region: Gondwana: central India and the Deccan fringes
entries.settlement: hill-and-forest seats (Garha, Deogarh) with textile and iron towns below
dwellings: fortified hill seats with mudbrick ramparts
entries.beliefs: Gond deities fused with the Hindu pantheon; clan deities (kula devas) central
entries.fell_by: Mughal pressure, Maratha partition, British annexation of Gondwana
entries.notes: One of India's largest tribal polities; Rani Durgavati's last stand against the Mughals is legend - 'brave heart' material.

entries.name: Toda people
entries.settlement: hamlets of three to seven thatched huts (munds) near buffalo pastures
crafts: embroidery (red and black on white cloth)
entries.beliefs: buffalo-centered animism; sacred dairies; a rich spirit world
entries.fell_by: not fallen; colonial plantation settlement transformed their pastures and herds
entries.notes: Strictly pastoral and non-agricultural until modern times; their barrel-vault hut is a distinctive voxel silhouette.

entries.name: Khasi people
entries.region: the Khasi and Jaintia hills, Meghalaya
climate: Cwb/Cfa extremely wet hills (among the wettest places on Earth)
entries.settlement: villages around stone-and-post clan houses (shnong); matrilineal clans
dwellings: raised bamboo houses on stone foundations
entries.beliefs: Khasi animism - U Blei (Sky God), forest and spring spirits, matrilineal clan rites
entries.fell_by: not fallen; annexed by the British in the 1830s after the Anglo-Khasi war
entries.notes: Matrilineal clans under a sky deity; living root bridges are their signature - a bioengineered block set piece.
